doc: The engines of the trip to the Moon (scripts/flight/transfer.gd). Each burn follows the rocket equation [S10]: the push is thrust / mass, and the mass falls by thrust / (Isp x g0) every second, so a burn starts gentle and ends hard. g0 = 9.80665 m/s2 (standard gravity, the same as data/parts.json).

departure.name: Departure stage
departure.desc: The rocket's last stage, still attached in the parking orbit: it fires the burn that sends the craft to the Moon, then is left behind.
departure.simplified: Apollo 11's S-IVB with its spacecraft. The mass is the combined vehicles in the parking orbit (297,914 lb) [S-afj11-tli]; the Isp is the J-2's in vacuum, 421 s [S-j2]. The thrust is ours, derived: the steady thrust that gives the game's 3,150 m/s in Apollo 11's 5 min 47 s with that mass and Isp (858 kN; the J-2 is rated 1,033 kN, and ran leaner for this burn). Real: 6.4 m/s2 at ignition, 13.6 m/s2 at cutoff.

craft.name: The craft's own engine
craft.desc: The spacecraft's main engine: the mid-course correction and the braking into lunar orbit.
craft.simplified: Apollo's Service Propulsion System, 91.19 kN and Isp 314.5 s [S-apollo-csm], on Apollo 11's 43,550 kg before the braking burn [S-afj11-loi]. With these, 889 m/s takes 369 s; Apollo 11's LOI-1 took 6 min 2 s (362 s). Real: 2.1 m/s2 at ignition.
